headline: South Africa Loses Agoa Eligibility, Threatening Citrus Exports
summary: Washington's plan to remove South Africa from Agoa in 2027 exposes citrus exports to tariffs, threatening orchards and jobs in the Western and Northern Cape.
why: The African Growth and Opportunity Act (Agoa) grants eligible sub-Saharan African nations duty-free access to the US market, making trade policy shifts critical for regional agricultural sectors.

impacts.name: South African Agriculture
impacts.why: Removal from Agoa eliminates tariff-free access for agricultural exports to the US.
